references.text: The same introductory formula is used throughout the book of Numbers, where the Lord speaks to Moses and gives him instructions for the people of Israel.
Nearly identical introductory formula in the same context regarding the allocation of land and settlement in Canaan.
Early reference to a place of refuge for someone who kills another unintentionally, which is further developed in Numbers 35.
Moses repeats and expands on the laws concerning cities of refuge that were given in Numbers 35.
The fulfillment of the command regarding cities of refuge that was given to Moses in Numbers 35.
The same Hebrew formula 'the Lord spoke to Moses and said' is used consistently throughout the books of Moses to introduce divine commands.
